sentences.text: Date of pronouncement: : 22.12.2025  AWAR D 1.
Proceedings in the present case arises from filing of DAR by the investigating officer in case FIR No. 278/2023 PS Mundka.

As per the DAR, documents filed therewith as well as material available on record, on 02.03.2023 at about 10:45 PM, at infront of Vinayak Green CNG Pump, PVC Road,
Tikri Kalan, Delhi, while Sh. Govind Kumar (hereinafter referred to as 'deceased') was pulling his Rehri/Rickshaw with engine and one Ajeet Pal was helping him to pull the Rehri/Rickshaw, in the meantime they were hit by the offending vehicle bearing no. HR-63-E-9508 (hereinafter referred to as 'offending vehicle) from back side.
The driver of the offending vehicle was driving the offending vehicle in a very rash and negligent manner and without obeying the traffic rules.
Thereafter the driver ran away with the bus and did not take care of the deceased.
It is further stated that deceased was taken to the Sanjay Gandhi Memorial Hospital, Mangolpuri, Delhi, where the postmortem of deceased was conducted vide PMR no. 219/23 dated 03.03.2023.
It is also stated that FIR bearing no. 278/2023 dated 03.03.2023 U/s 279/304 A IPC was got registered relating to the incident in question.

2. As per the DAR alongwith the documents filed therewith, respondent no. 1 is the driver of the offending vehicle;
MACT No. 494/2023 Date of Award : 22.12.2025 Ramdhun & Ors Vs. Sanjiv & Ors.
Page No. 2/23.
respondent no.2 is the registered owner of the offending vehicle and the respondent no.3 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.

In the written statement filed on behalf of respondent no. 1 and 2, it is stated inter alia that the offending vehicle is duly insured with the respondent no. 3 vide insurance policy no.
1112053122P105682629 valid upto 16.09.2022 to 15.09.2022.
It is further stated that the deceased would have met with the accident with some other vehicle due to his own negligence.

It is further stated that respondent no. 1 has been falsely implicated by the police officials and no accident as alleged in the petition had occurred with the vehicle of the respondent no. 2.
4.

In its reply filed on behalf of the insurance company/respondent no. 3, it is stated inter alia that the rickshaw is modified one i.e engine/motor is installed in it which is illegal and not valid as per law.
It is further stated that deceased have smashed into the alleged offending vehicle.
It is further stated that the deceased was travelling in a modified rickshaw which is illegal and not valid.

It is further stated the offending vehicle was not in perfect road worthy condition and in violation of rules and regulations as the time of alleged accident, the offending MACT No. 494/2023 Date of Ramdhun And Ors vs Sanjiv And Ors on 22 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/87272107/

It is further stated that offending vehicle HR-63-E-9508 (Bus) was insured with the respondent no. 3 w.e.f 16.09.2022 to midnight of 15.09.2023.
5.

From the pleadings of the parties, following issues were framed by the Ld. Predecessor of this Tribunal on 21.11.2023 :-
1.

Whether the deceased Govind Kumar suffered fatal injuries in a vehicular accident that took place on 02.03.2023 at 10:45 PM in front of Vinayak Green CNG Pump,
PVC Road, Tikri Kalan, Delhi involving a vehicle No. HR-63-E-9508 (offending vehicle) being driven by respondent no. 1 Sanjiv, owned by respondent no. 2 Jasbir and insured by respondent no. 3 United India Insurance Co. Ltd?
OPP 2.Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation?
If so, to what amount and from whom?

3. Relief.
6.
In order to prove their case, petitioners got examined three witnesses.

PW-1 is petitioner no.1 Sh. Ramdhun (father of deceased); PW-2 Sh. Shalem and PW 3 Sh.
Anoop Kumar, who are stated to be the eye-witnesses of the incident in question.
7. Respondent no. 1 has examined himself as R1W1.
In respondent evidence on behalf of respondent no. 3 one witness R3/W1 was examined.

8. I have heard arguments advanced by Ld. Counsel for the parties and gone through the record carefully and my issue wise findings are as under :
Issue No.1 MACT No. 494/2023 Date of Award : 22.12.2025 Ramdhun & Ors Vs.
Sanjiv & Ors.

9. It is the settled proposition of law that an action founded on the principle of fault liability, the proof of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is sine qua non.
However, the standard of proof is not as strict as applied in criminal cases and evidence is to be tested on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities.
Holistic view is to be taken while dealing with the Claim Petition based upon negligence.
Strict rules of evidence are not applicable in an inquiry conducted by the Claims Tribunal.

Reference may be made to the judgments titled as New India Assurance Co. Ltd. v.
Sakshi Bhutani & Others., MAC APP. No. 550/2011 decided on 02.07.2012, Bimla Devi & Others v.
Himachal Road Transport Corporation & Others (2009) 13 SC 530, Parmeshwari v. Amirchand &
Others 2011 (1) SCR 1096 & Mangla Ram v. Oriental Insurance Company Ltd. & Others 2018, Law Suit (SC) 303.

13 . It is quite evident that the presence of PW-2 and PW-3 at the spot is duly established.
PW-2 and PW-3 have categorically deposed in their cross examination that on 02.03.2023 after selling the vegetables, they proceed to Tikri Border from Geetanjali and they have seen the accident.
They have also described the entire mode and manner of the accident in question in detail and police recorded the statement of PW 3 Sh. Anoop Kumar.
PW-2 and PW-3 were cross examined at length

, however,
there is nothing material elicited from their cross examination, which would impeach their credibility or trustworthiness.
PW-2 is independent public witness, has given the true account of whatever took place in his presence at the spot at the time of accident.
There is no reason to disbelieve the version of accident given by him.
There is no reason as to why they depose falsely against the respondent no. 1.
There is no possibility of false implication of respondent no. 1 and/or false involvement of offending vehicle by PW-3 at the instance of petitioners herein.
Plea of the respondent no. 3 that it was deceased who was negligent due to which accident caused, has not been substantiated by any cogent evidence.

14. Ld. Counsel for respondent no. 3/Insurance Company has argued that charge-sheet was filed by the IO for offence U/s 279/304A IPC and there is lack of proof of rashness and negligence on the part of driver of the offending vehicle and therefore, insurance co. is not liable for compensation.

It is also argued by the Ld. Counsel for the respondents that petitioners have failed to establish that deceased received fatal injuries due to the alleged rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle by the respondent no. 1.
Per contra, Ld. Counsel for the petitioners MACT No. 494/2023 Date of Award : 22.12.2025 Ramdhun & Ors Vs. Sanjiv & Ors.

He has also relied on the Judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case titled "Rita Devi & Ors. Vs. New India Assurance Co. sentences.text: In the facts of the present case, from careful examining the evidence of PW2 and PW 3 who were present at the spot, no doubt it came in their evidence that vehicle was being driven in rash and negligent manner by respondent no.1 Sanjiv.

When it is proved from the evidence of PW2 and PW 3 that the vehicle in question was being driven in a rash and negligent manner and the driver of the said offending vehicle has also been prosecuted for rash and negligent driving.
That fact itself is sufficient for concluding regarding rash and negligent driving of respondent no. 1.

Moreover, plea of the respondent no. 3 that it was the deceased who was negligent due to which accident was caused or that he contributed to the causing of accident, has not been substantiated by any cogent evidence.

16. Respondent no. 1 got himself examined, who deposed that he was working as a driver on 02.03.2023 on bus no. HR-63-E-9508 which was plied on the route from Rohtak, MACT No.

the e- rickshaw driver lost his control and hit the unknown vehicle and thereafter hit the stationary bus of the respondent no. 1 from the front side; that the accident took place due to the negligence of the unknown vehicle and e-rickshaw driver (deceased) and there was no fault on the part of respondent no. 1 whose bus was stationary and parked on Kaccha road inside the CNG station; that at the time of occurrence of the accident, the bus of respondent no. 1 was not in use nor in motion nor carrying any passenger and required repair and fuel.

sentences.text: On the basis of material available on record, it is duly established that respondent no. 1 was driving the offending vehicle at the time of accident.

In these circumstances as well as material available on record, the deposition of respondent no. 1 does not offers any help to him in any manner much less to absolve him of his culpability in the commission of offence in the present case.

19. Moreover, as per the postmortem report of deceased Govind Kumar vide P. M. Report No.
219/23 dated 03.03.2023 filed by the IO alongwith present DAR, the opinion therein is given as "The cause of death is hemorrhagic shock as a result of abdominal injury due to blunt force impact.
All injuries are antemortem in nature and possible in manner as alleged".
Said document has not been disputed from the side of the respondents and corroborates the ocular testimony of PW2 and PW3.
MACT No. 494/2023 Date of Award : 22.12.2025 Ramdhun & Ors Vs. Sanjiv & Ors.
Page No. 11/23.

20 . Thus, in view of the aforesaid discussion and the evidence which has come on record, it is held that the petitioners have been able to prove on the basis of preponderance of probabilities that deceased Govind Kumar sustained fatal injuries in road accident which took place on 02.03.2023 at about 10:45 PM, at infront of Vinayak Green CNG Pump, PVC Road, Tikri Kalan, Delhi, due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle by the respondent no. 1.
Accordingly issue no.1 stands decided in favour of petitioners and against the respondents.
Issue No.2 21.
In view of the finding on issue no. 1, petitioners are entitled to get compensation, however, the quantum of compensation still needs to be adjudicated.

Section 168 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 enjoins upon the claim Tribunal to hold an inquiry into the claim to make an award determining the amount of compensation, which appears to be just and reasonable.
As per settled law, compensation is not expected to be windfall or a bonanza nor it should be pittance.
A man is not compensated for the physical injury, he is compensated for the loss which he suffers as a result of that injury.
Computation of Compensation 22.
The present case pertains to the death of deceased Govind Kumar.

In death cases, the guidelines for computation of compensation have been laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Sarla Verma and Others v. Delhi Transport Corporation & Anr. (2009) 6 Supreme Court Cases 121.

To counter the arguments of Ld. Counsel for respondent no. 3, Ld. Counsel for the petitioners had argued that DAR is admissible in evidence at its face value as no contradictory reliable material to doubt the contents of the DAR or documents filed with it, have been brought on record by any of the respondents.
He has further argued that it is the duty of the insurance company to get the DAR verified by their surveyor.

The main contention of Ld. Counsel for the respondent no. 3/insurance company is that petitioners are not having any documentary proof to show that Govind Kumar (deceased) was a resident of Delhi or was working in Delhi and that his Aadhar card produced on record is having address of Uttar Pradesh and as such the minimum wages applicable in Uttar Pradesh at the time of incident in question should be taken into consideration, while deciding the factor of income of deceased.
I have carefully gone through the material available on record.
26. The persons engaged in the unorganized sector ordinarily do not have or keep records or proof of their employment or earnings.
Therefore, strict rules of evidence would not be applicable to such parties, like the petitioners to prove by documentary evidence that the deceased was working and earning in Delhi.
In view of the aforesaid discussion and in view of the judgment of Hon'ble High Court titled as Babu & Ors. Vs. Vikas Duggal & Ors.

It is also not disputed that when the offending bus entered Delhi it was not being plied to ferry passengers.
The purpose of entering in Delhi was to get the CNG filled from the neighboring area to enable the bus to run which was not possible without fuel.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
However, the standard of proof is not as strict as applied in criminal cases and evidence is to be tested on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities.
Holistic view is to be taken while dealing with the Claim Petition based upon negligence.
Strict rules of evidence are not applicable in an inquiry conducted by the Claims Tribunal.
Reference may be made to the judgments titled as New India Assurance Co. Ltd. v.
Sakshi Bhutani & Others., MAC APP. No. 550/2011 decided on 02.07.2012, Bimla Devi & Others v.
Himachal Road Transport Corporation & Others (2009) 13 SC 530, Parmeshwari v. Amirchand &
Others 2011 (1) SCR 1096 & Mangla Ram v. Oriental Insurance Company Ltd. & Others 2018, Law Suit (SC) 303.
Ramdhun
PW-2 is independent public witness, has given the true account of whatever took place in his presence at the spot at the time of accident.
There is no reason to disbelieve the version of accident given by him.
There is no reason as to why they depose falsely against the respondent no. 1.
There is no possibility of false implication of respondent no. 1 and/or false involvement of offending vehicle by PW-3 at the instance of petitioners herein.
Plea of the respondent no. 3 that it was deceased who was negligent due to which accident caused, has not been substantiated by any cogent evidence.
When it is proved from the evidence of PW2 and PW 3 that the vehicle in question was being driven in a rash and negligent manner and the driver of the said offending vehicle has also been prosecuted for rash and negligent driving.
Moreover, plea of the respondent no. 3 that it was the deceased who was negligent due to which accident was caused or that he contributed to the causing of accident, has not been substantiated by any cogent evidence.
In view of the finding on issue no. 1, petitioners are entitled to get compensation, however, the quantum of compensation still needs to be adjudicated.
Section 168 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 enjoins upon the claim Tribunal to hold an inquiry into the claim to make an award determining the amount of compensation, which appears to be just and reasonable.
As per settled law, compensation is not expected to be windfall or a bonanza nor it should be pittance.
A man is not compensated for the physical injury, he is compensated for the loss which he suffers as a result of that injury.
Computation of Compensation 22.
In death cases, the guidelines for computation of compensation have been laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Sarla Verma and Others v. Delhi Transport Corporation & Anr. (2009) 6 Supreme Court Cases 121.
Further, the guidelines have been reiterated by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in a case titled as National Insurance Company vs. Pranay Sethi & Ors., 2017 ACJ 2700, decided on 31.10.2017, laying down the general MACT No. 494/2023 Date of Award : 22.12.2025 Ramdhun & Ors Vs. Sanjiv &
Ors. Page No. 12/23. principles for computation of compensation in death cases.
26. The persons engaged in the unorganized sector ordinarily do not have or keep records or proof of their employment or earnings.
Therefore, strict rules of evidence would not be applicable to such parties, like the petitioners to prove by documentary evidence that the deceased was working and earning in Delhi.
Tribunal is of the considered opinion that Govind Kumar (deceased) was working as labourer in Delhi at the time of accident i.e. 02.03.2023.
With regard to the aspect of earning of Rs. 30,000/- per month by Govind Kumar (deceased), the petitioners have failed to bring on record any income certificate or salary slip of the deceased.
The deceased was working as labour and the award should be granted as per the minimum wages of unskilled in Delhi at the time of accident.
Respondent No. 3/Insurance company has taken specific plea of violation of terms of the insurance policy as it came that the offending vehicle was a commercial vehicle and had the permit route from Tikri Boarder to Rohtak but respondent no. 1 entered into Delhi without having any valid permit to enter into Delhi.

Therefore there can be no presumption drawn regarding due service of notice upon respondent on. 1 and 2.

the statement containing FDR number, FDR amount, date of maturity and maturity amount shall be furnished by bank to the claimant.

(g) The bank shall make an endorsement on the passbook of the claimant to the effect that no cheque book and/or debit card have been issued and shall not be issued without the permission of the Court and claimant shall produce the passbook with the necessary endorsement before the Court on the next date fixed for compliance.
